newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore telecom authority in licenses offer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore telecom authority in licenses offer.

text.p: The Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) said on Friday it would allow the resale of leased circuit services from February 1.
The move means firms can lease services from Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) and sell them on to customers for intra-corporate communications, said a TAS statement.
SingTel currently has exclusive rights to lease circuit services until March 31, 2000.
TAS said the move would see more competitive pricing and wider ranges of services available to business customers.
Leased circuits are designed for users with high volumes of calls, enabling them to create private dedicated intra-corporation communications links.
TAS said companies wanting to resell or share leased circuits must apply for a license. Leased circuits would not be allowed to be connected to public switched networks.

TAS said licenses would be valid for one year and renewable annually. Costs will include a one-time fee of Singapore $50,000 and an annual fee of one percent of annual gross turnover or S$10,000, whichever is higher.
